title: arXiv Mathematics — notable papers from the Fri 23 Oct 2026 batch
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart; ordering is inferred, not measured popularity. Semantic Scholar currently reports zero citations for each of these six fresh papers, so citation evidence is too sparse to measure short-window attention.

sections.title: No Perfect Randomized Composition
sections.abstract: The paper constructs total Boolean functions whose randomized query complexity under composition is smaller than the product of the two component complexities by a logarithmic factor, and develops related separations among query-complexity measures.
sections.claimed_result: The author constructs total Boolean functions with R(f∘g) = Θ(R(f)R(g)/log R(g)), refuting a constant-factor product lower bound for total-function composition; the paper also gives further separations among related query measures.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Bounded-error randomized query complexity of block compositions of total Boolean functions; the exhibited separation is logarithmic and uses carefully coupled input sizes.
sections.unique_caveat: The author explicitly notes that this does not refute composition up to polylogarithmic factors; the large separation depends on the construction's scale relationship.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Concrete counterexample to a standard composition principle; cross-listed between computational complexity and combinatorics; same-day Theory of Computing Report item; abstract reports a Lean formalization.

sections.title: Lenses make many points: Pure point spectrum disproves Simon's L2 conjecture
sections.abstract: For every dimension d ≥ 2 and 0 ≤ σ < 1/3, the authors construct smooth, bounded, nonnegative potentials with arbitrarily small stated weighted norms for which the Schrödinger operator has pure point spectrum throughout positive energies.
sections.claimed_result: Becker and Yang claim that their potentials have no continuous spectral component on [0,∞), disproving the stated Simon conjecture; Theorem 1.1 gives the construction under the stronger weighted condition for every σ < 1/3.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Schrödinger operators −Δ+V on R^d, d ≥ 2; V is smooth, bounded and nonnegative, with both the unweighted and additional |x|^σ-weighted radial L2 quantities arbitrarily small.
sections.unique_caveat: The weight range stops below σ = 1/3; the paper discloses LLM assistance in developing the construction, so independent scrutiny of the full proof is especially important. This report has not checked the proof.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Explicit counterexample to a named spectral conjecture; cross-listed in spectral theory and mathematical physics; surfaced in a same-day spectral-theory research feed and indexed in a MathWorld entry about the conjecture/result.

sections.title: Conway's thrackle conjecture: a new upper bound of 4/3 n
sections.abstract: The author proves that a thrackleable graph with n ≥ 4 vertices has at most floor(4(n−1)/3) edges, combining a finite computer-assisted result with discharging arguments in plane and projective-plane embeddings.
sections.claimed_result: Simon proves m ≤ floor(4(n−1)/3) for every thrackleable graph on n ≥ 4 vertices.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite simple graphs admitting a plane drawing in which each pair of edges meets exactly once, either at a shared endpoint or a proper crossing; the proof combines discharging with verification of the conjectured bound for graphs up to 12 vertices.
sections.unique_caveat: The new upper bound remains above Conway's conjectured m ≤ n, so the conjecture is not settled; the proof relies on the cited computer-assisted finite verification.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Sharper explicit bound on a long-standing conjecture; cross-listed across combinatorics, general mathematics, and geometric topology; the introduction compares it with the preceding 18/13-type bound.

sections.title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in F_p^d for p=2,d=8 and p=11,d=3
sections.abstract: The authors prove the finite-group tile/spectral equivalence in F₂⁸ and F₁₁³, and give substantial additional structure and reductions for spectral sets in F₂⁹.
sections.claimed_result: Ferguson and Iosevich prove Fuglede's conjecture for F₂⁸ and F₁₁³; for F₂⁹ they show every tile is spectral, every spectral set has power-of-two size, and all spectral cardinalities other than 64 tile.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Nonempty subsets of finite vector spaces F_p^d; spectral means admitting an orthogonal character spectrum, while tiles means tiling the group by translations.
sections.unique_caveat: These are finite-group results, not a resolution of Fuglede's conjecture in general; the abstract leaves the cardinality-64 case in F₂⁹ for further work.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Resolves two specific cases of a central harmonic-analysis conjecture; contributes reductions in a neighboring dimension; described computational verification programs are among ancillary materials.

sections.title: Non-uniqueness for the forced one-dimensional Vlasov-Poisson equation
sections.abstract: For every finite p, the author constructs two distinct distributional solutions with the same zero initial data for a forced one-dimensional Vlasov–Poisson problem, while proving uniqueness in the stated Lipschitz-field class when the spatial density is bounded.
sections.claimed_result: Iacobelli constructs a nonnegative source and two nonnegative solutions in C([0,1];L1(R2)) with the same zero data and uniformly Lp(R) spatial densities for every finite p; in the Lipschitz-electric-field class, bounded spatial density restores uniqueness.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Forced one-dimensional Vlasov–Poisson equation on the whole space; the source is continuous in time with values in L1(R2) and vanishes initially, and the ion density is smooth for positive times.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is for a forced one-dimensional problem with the constructed source; it does not assert nonuniqueness for the unforced equation or higher-dimensional settings.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract states a sharp contrast between nonuniqueness for every finite Lp density bound and uniqueness for bounded density, a precise well-posedness threshold rather than a qualitative example.

sections.title: Collapsed translating solitons with planar wings
sections.abstract: For complete embedded translators in R³ with finite genus and finite entropy, the authors prove that a collapsed translator with all wings of planar type must be a vertical plane, and classify the collapsed finite-genus case below entropy 3.
sections.claimed_result: Gama, Martín, and Møller claim planar-wing rigidity for collapsed translators and a full classification of collapsed embedded finite-genus translators with entropy λ < 3.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Complete embedded translating solitons in R³, finite genus and finite entropy; the rigidity statement additionally assumes collapsed ends whose wings are all planar in the authors' weak topological sense.
sections.unique_caveat: The rigidity hypothesis restricts the geometry of the ends, and the stated classification is limited to entropy below 3; it does not classify all translating solitons.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A rigidity theorem with a classification corollary and a sharp exterior decay estimate as a named technical ingredient; placed after broader conjecture and bound results because independent attention evidence is thinner.
